question: K8 (8-bit) measured worse than K6 (6-bit) on panel window final-0000, same lane, same estimator. Is the K8 checkpoint defective, or is it mis-measured?

verdict.cause: UNDERPOWERED COMPARISON - a single-window sampling artifact
verdict.one_line: K8 is not worse. It is better. The comparison was made on one window of a 25-window panel, and per-window mean KLD is heavy-tailed enough that a single window cannot distinguish the two rates. Across all 11 windows captured by both runs, K8 wins 9 of 11 and is better in pooled mean, pooled median and top-1 agreement.
verdict.action: Compare on the full sealed panel, never on one window.

the_window_the_anomaly_was_seen_on.note: reproduced independently to ~1.6e-8 of the reported values

all_windows_captured_by_both_runs.interpretation: K8's advantage is ~2.3 standard errors with 11 windows. The per-window spread (sd 1.73e-3) is LARGER than the effect (1.22e-3), so a single window has no power to separate the rates - which is exactly how window-0000 produced the false alarm.

sealed_reference_consistency.note: our 11-window K6 pooled mean is within 1.5e-4 of the sealed 25-window number, so the 11-window subsample is representative

why_one_window_is_not_enough.observation: per-position KLD is extremely heavy-tailed; a window's MEAN is dominated by a handful of positions

window_0000_excess_decomposition.meaning: the 8 worst positions account for MORE than the entire excess; removing them flips window-0000 to a K8 win

drop_k_worst_positions_window_0000.drop_8: K8 becomes competitive; the deficit is entirely outlier-driven

quantile_evidence_window_0000.note: even on the ADVERSE window, K8 is better in the upper tail; the loss comes from a few extreme positions plus a slightly worse median

shipped_store_reconstruction_error.description: THE decisive artifact-quality measurement: ||W_hat - W||/||W|| of the ACTUAL SHIPPED payload stores vs BF16, with the intermediate-channel permutation undone
shipped_store_reconstruction_error.conclusion: The shipped K8 store is not merely acceptable - it is substantially tighter than K6, exactly as 8 bits should be. The artifact is sound.

the_intermediate_channel_permutation.status: IDENTIFIED - this unblocked the measurement above
the_intermediate_channel_permutation.what_it_is: the campaign encodes each expert in a permuted intermediate-channel frame. Permuting gate_proj/up_proj output rows and down_proj input columns by the SAME permutation leaves the expert's function unchanged, so serving is unaffected.

evidence.reading: identical magnitude multisets, scrambled positions - a permutation, not noise
evidence.recovered_by: matching decoded intermediate-channel rows to BF16 rows by cosine
evidence.bijection: 2048 of 2048 unique targets on every projection tested
evidence.same_perm_across_projections: the permutation recovered from gate_proj, applied unchanged to up_proj and down_proj, yields the expected error - confirming the symmetry is applied consistently within each expert
evidence.same_perm_across_campaigns: perm(K6) == perm(K8) for 10 of 10 experts, consistent with same_transform_seed_as_k6_campaign

the_intermediate_channel_permutation.why_it_looked_like_noise: cos(|W_hat|,|W|) = 0.6328, and 2/pi = 0.6366 is exactly the value for two independent Gaussians of equal variance - which is what a random permutation of the same magnitude multiset produces
the_intermediate_channel_permutation.this_was_the_blocker: reported in v1 as an unresolved instrumentation problem; now resolved

test_1_reader_k8_decode.route_b: exllamav3 @ c5d9c657 native CUDA kernel ext.reconstruct
test_1_reader_k8_decode.levels: both pre-Hadamard (trellis unpack + MCG codebook) and post-Hadamard (sign/scale)
test_1_reader_k8_decode.conclusion: 128-word K8 trellis tiles, bit-packing stride and tail handling are all correct; patch 0007's parametric claim holds

test_2_transform_convention.conclusion: decode is the exact algebraic inverse of the encoder; no sign/scale mismatch

test_3_fresh_encode_on_real_experts.conclusion: the codec genuinely delivers at 8 bits

test_4_profile.result: K6 and K8 used a BYTE-IDENTICAL fixed default profile
test_4_profile.conclusion: the 'K8 got an untuned profile' hypothesis is false

test_5_measurement_lane.result: the two run plans are identical in every measurement-relevant field

test_7_materialized_checkpoint.result: ckpt-k8 trellis/suh/svh are byte-identical to the out-k8 payload store
test_7_materialized_checkpoint.conclusion: the published checkpoint and the measured store are the same artifact

hypotheses_final_status.shipped_k8_store_underperforms_its_rate: ELIMINATED - it is 13.2x tighter than K6
hypotheses_final_status.downstream_surface_assembly_fault: ELIMINATED - no fault to explain; K8 wins on the panel

guidance: Publish the K8 artifact normally. It is a genuine improvement over K6: 13.2x tighter weights and a lower panel KLD (0.01266 vs 0.01387 pooled over 11 windows), with higher top-1 agreement (96.34% vs 96.12%).
Do NOT quote single-window KLD as a rate comparison. Per-window deltas have sd 1.73e-3 against an effect of 1.22e-3, so one window is pure noise. Quote the sealed full-panel number.
Let the in-flight K8 run finish all 25 windows and compare against the sealed 25-window K6 number (0.0137234) for the published figure.
Consider adding a trimmed or median KLD alongside the mean in future reports; per-position KLD is heavy-tailed enough that a few positions dominate any window mean.
Document the intermediate-channel permutation in the campaign notes: any future weight-space audit against BF16 must undo it, or it will look like the store is noise.

environment.neighbour_policy: all work nice -n 19, no processes killed, nothing written under out-k6/out-k8/stream-k6/stream-k8/receipts/ckpt-k8
